summary:
I verified 131 YouTube videos end-to-end by actually downloading their Japanese caption tracks (HTTP 200 + real cue text inspected), spread N5:30 / N4:22 / N3:21 / N2:34 / N1:24 — every one has a MANUAL (human-written) Japanese track, and 63 also have a manual English track. Two build-pipeline gotchas the shared context did not have: (1) the ANDROID-client `baseUrl` already carries `fmt=srv3`, so appending `&fmt=json3` is silently ignored — you must overwrite the param with `URL.searchParams.set("fmt","json3")` or you get XML; (2) the timedtext endpoint rate-limits hard with HTTP 429 after roughly 200-300 fetches and the block persisted over 30 minutes, so the bake pipeline must be serial with exponential backoff and resumable. I also confirmed caption URLs are signed and expire in ~7 hours, which forces build-time baking, and that `playabilityStatus.playableInEmbed` is the pre-flight embed check. The single biggest design constraint I found is legal: YouTube's Required Minimum Functionality terms say "You must not display overlays, frames, or other visual elements in front of any part of a YouTube embedded player" — so the big subtitles must render BELOW the iframe, not on top of it. That happens to also solve the iOS native-fullscreen problem and gives far better phone ergonomics. Tapping a Japanese word requires build-time tokenization (kuromoji's dictionary is 17MB, far too big to ship); kuromoji gives `basic_form`, so tapping conjugated 起き resolves to 起きる for JMdict lookup. Business/workplace Japanese is the one gap: I found 48 excellent candidates with confirmed manual JA tracks (Meshclass, Native Dojo, Moshi Moshi Rico Sensei, plus folktales and N1 JLPT prep) but the 429 block stopped me downloading their cue bodies, so I have listed them separately as unverified rather than mixing them into the verified array.</summary>

For a 'big text' mode, grow the panel and shrink the video, do not go fullscreen.","why":"YouTube's Required Minimum Functionality terms state verbatim: 'You must not display overlays, frames, or other visual elements in front of any part of a YouTube embedded player, including player controls' and 'Embedded players must have a viewport that is at least 200px by 200px.' The cursor hint makes the common case O(1) instead of O(log n) on a 2000-cue file.","priority":"high"},{"title":"Tap-to-pause is safe; tap-to-play is not","decision":"Call pauseVideo() freely from a word tap. Only ever call playVideo() from inside a real user gesture handler, and always set playerVars.playsinline=1. Never attempt autoplay unless muted.","why":"Browser autoplay policies gate PLAY, not PAUSE — so the flagship 'tap any word to pause and get an explanation' interaction works cleanly with no gesture problems. Conversely playsinline=1 is mandatory or iOS hijacks playback into native fullscreen, which would hide your whole UI.","priority":"must-have"},{"title":"Align JA and EN cues by max-overlap ownership, not by index","decision":"Use the supplied align() function: each EN cue is assigned to the single JA cue it overlaps most (its owner); each JA cue shows the concatenated text of the EN cues it owns; a JA cue owning nothing borrows the EN cue with largest overlap and is flagged enShared so the UI can dim it.","why":"JA and EN tracks are authored independently and their boundaries never match — Japanese cues are typically shorter and denser. Naive index pairing desynchronises within seconds. I unit-tested this algorithm on deliberately mismatched cues: one EN cue spanning two JA cues is owned by the larger overlap and merely borrowed by the other, and a JA cue past the end of the EN track correctly yields null rather than a wrong translation. Add a CI job that oembed-pings every catalog ID weekly and flags dead ones.","why":"I verified oembed returns 200 with title/author for a live video and 400 for a nonexistent one, making it a clean binary health check. The crucial design win is that baking decouples your content from YouTube's availability — losing a video costs you the audio, not the lesson. Also check playabilityStatus.playableInEmbed at bake time (verified present and true) so you never ship a video that refuses to embed.","priority":"high"},{"title":"Prefer short N5 videos as the on-ramp and long dense ones as mining sources","decision":"Open each level with its shortest videos (SvzCKlfD5mw is 2:40/24 cues; fURDk5MNOXI is 2:51/23 cues) and surface the 1000+ cue files (QruEgF-IQO0 2057 cues, MBDuDe5rJOQ 1029, IN_C2s8W0eY 890) as 'vocabulary mining' sessions rather than lessons.","why":"A complete beginner who opens a 62-minute video quits. verified_facts.claim: The innertube ANDROID-client player endpoint returns caption track metadata for arbitrary video IDs from this machine
verified_facts.evidence: POST https://www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/player?key=AIzaSy... with clientName ANDROID / clientVersion 20.10.38 returned HTTP 200 for all 568 round-1 candidates and all 645 round-2 candidates (1213 videos, zero failures). Example: dQw4w9WgXcQ -> playabilityStatus OK, captionTracks [en:manual, en:asr, de-DE:manual, ja:manual, pt-BR:manual, es-419:manual].

verified_facts.evidence:
baseUrl query params printed as: v,ei,caps,opi,xoaf,xowf,hl,ip,ipbits,expire,sparams,signature,key,lang,fmt with fmt=srv3. GET baseUrl+'&fmt=json3' -> HTTP 200, Content-Type text/xml; charset=UTF-8, 2449 bytes, body '

verified_facts.claim: 131 videos were verified by actually downloading their Japanese caption track and inspecting real cue text
verified_facts.evidence: Each recorded 'json3 HTTP 200 bytes=N cues=N' plus sampled cue text. Examples: T_5sjgI83kc HTTP 200 bytes=5817 cues=49 sample '私は日本人です。'; Pp52_2wi-Gg HTTP 200 bytes=11715 cues=106 sample 'でも今、娘は飴が食べられません。'; MBDuDe5rJOQ HTTP 200 bytes=110114 cues=1029 sample '人と人とのコミュニケーションが'; Lf8oNdG4EQI HTTP 200 bytes=67564 cues=545; QruEgF-IQO0 2057 cues. All 131 have jaTrack=manual (no 'kind' field on the track).

verified_facts.claim: Sampled caption text is real, sensibly segmented Japanese whose difficulty matches the claimed level
verified_facts.evidence: Computed a Japanese-character ratio per video (kana+kanji / total chars); the 131 range 0.65-0.99, most above 0.85. Level sanity confirmed by reading samples: N5 dc8T-q213tg gives '青ですか？'; N3 f5FT4G0tJg8 gives 'はい、１つ目の便利なキッチングッズは、場所を取らず衛生的なしゃもじです。'; N1 7MjboLBgzbM gives '空気が読めないと「KY」って言われたりします。'; N1 88TbLNnaPgI gives '自分が実際に過去に経験したことを元に、現実的なものの見方、考え方をするのが感覚型の人たちです。'

verified_facts.claim: The timedtext endpoint rate-limits with HTTP 429 and the block persists for a long time
verified_facts.evidence: A concurrency-8 run over 645 videos returned 'json3 HTTP 429' for all 586 videos that had a JA track, while the player endpoint returned 200 for all 645 in the same run. Retrying serially at 2.6s spacing with backoff 1.5s->30s over 6 attempts still gave '429 exhausted'. A single manual probe more than 30 minutes later still returned 429. 523 of those 586 were confirmed to carry manual JA tracks.

verified_facts.claim: Caption baseUrls are signed and expire in about 7 hours, so they cannot be stored in the app
verified_facts.evidence: For G-ArHStBCN8 the baseUrl expire param was 1789983957 = 2026-09-21T09:45:57Z, i.e. 7.0 hours ahead of fetch time, and the URL carries signature and sparams=ip,ipbits,expire,v,ei,caps,opi,xoaf,xowf params.

verified_facts.claim: playabilityStatus.playableInEmbed is available at bake time as an embed pre-flight check
verified_facts.evidence: For G-ArHStBCN8 the player response gave playableInEmbed: true, isPrivate: false, isLiveContent: false.

verified_facts.claim: oembed is a reliable liveness check for catalog maintenance
verified_facts.evidence: GET https://www.youtube.com/oembed?url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G-ArHStBCN8&format=json -> HTTP 200 with title 'Comprehensible Japanese - Morning Routin...'. Same call with a nonexistent id 'aaaaaaaaaaa' -> HTTP 400.

verified_facts.claim: YouTube's terms forbid overlaying anything in front of an embedded player and set a 200x200 minimum viewport
verified_facts.evidence: https://developers.google.com/youtube/terms/required-minimum-functionality states 'You must not display overlays, frames, or other visual elements in front of any part of a YouTube embedded player, including player controls' and 'Embedded players must have a viewport that is at least 200px by 200px', recommending 480x270 for 16:9.

verified_facts.claim: kuromoji tokenizes Japanese correctly and supplies dictionary base forms, but its dictionary is far too large to ship
verified_facts.evidence: npm install kuromoji; du -sh node_modules/kuromoji/dict -> 17M. Tokenizing 毎朝六時に起きて、コーヒーを飲みながら新聞を読んでいます。 yielded 起き (base=起きる, pos=動詞/自立, read=オキ, conj=連用形), 飲み (base=飲む), 読ん (base=読む), plus correct particle/auxiliary tagging. Keigo input 本日はお忙しい中、お越しいただきありがとうございます。 tokenized with ござい -> base ござる.

verified_facts.claim: The JA/EN cue alignment algorithm handles mismatched boundaries, shared translations and missing English correctly
verified_facts.evidence: Unit test with 6 JA cues against 3 longer EN cues: 'Good morning.' (0-2800ms) was owned by おはよう (overlap 1500) and only borrowed by ございます (flagged shared); 'It is. Shall we go for a walk?' (6300-11800) was owned by 散歩に行きましょうか (overlap 4800) not そうですね (overlap 700); trailing うん with no EN overlap returned null. Running align(ja, []) returned every cue with en:null rather than throwing.

verified_facts.claim: YouTube search via innertube with the closed-caption filter is an effective way to harvest candidates
verified_facts.evidence: POST /youtubei/v1/search with params 'EgIoAQ%3D%3D' (CC filter) returned ~20 results per query; 78 queries produced 1213 unique video IDs, of which 242 in round 1 alone had manual JA tracks with successfully downloaded cues.

verified_facts.claim: 48 business/story/N1 candidates have confirmed manual Japanese caption tracks but their cue bodies were NOT downloaded
verified_facts.evidence: All 48 returned playabilityStatus OK from the player API with a ja track lacking the 'kind' field (= manual); 36 also list a manual en track. Their timedtext fetches all returned 429. These are listed separately in code_or_data as businessAndStoryCandidates and must be verified before shipping.

verified_facts.claim: pauseVideo() is not gesture-restricted while playVideo() is, and playsinline=1 is required on iOS
verified_facts.evidence: https://developers.google.com/youtube/iframe_api_reference documents autoplay policies applying to playback initiation and an onAutoplayBlocked event; player_parameters documents playsinline=1 as causing inline playback on iOS. Community reports (Apple Developer Forums thread 713772, humhub issue 2303) confirm omitting playsinline causes iOS to take over with native fullscreen.

/* ============================================================================
   4. align.mjs - JA/EN cue alignment (unit-tested, see verified_facts)
   ============================================================================ */
export function toCues(json3){
  const evs=(json3.events||[]).filter(e=>e.segs&&e.segs.some(s=>(s.utf8||"").trim()));
  const cues=evs.map(e=>({
    s:e.tStartMs,
    e:e.tStartMs+(e.dDurationMs??0),
    t:e.segs.map(s=>s.utf8).join("").replace(/\s+/g," ").trim()
  })).filter(c=>c.t);
  for(let i=0;i<cues.length;i++){
    // json3 sometimes omits dDurationMs -> derive the end from the next start
    if(!(cues[i].e>cues[i].s)) cues[i].e = i+1<cues.length ? cues[i+1].s : cues[i].s+2000;
    // ASR tracks emit rolling, overlapping cues - clamp so lookup stays unambiguous
    if(i+1<cues.length && cues[i].e>cues[i+1].s) cues[i].e=cues[i+1].s;
  }
  return cues;
}
const ov=(a,b)=>Math.max(0,Math.min(a.e,b.e)-Math.max(a.s,b.s));

/* ALGORITHM
   JA and EN tracks are authored independently, so their cue boundaries never match.
   Index-pairing desyncs immediately. Instead:
   Pass 1 - OWNERSHIP: walk the EN cues (both tracks are time-sorted, so keep a
            moving pointer into JA). Each EN cue is assigned to the ONE JA cue it
            overlaps most in time. That JA cue "owns" it. An EN cue is owned once.
   Pass 2 - EMIT: a JA cue renders the concatenation of the EN cues it owns.
            A JA cue that owns nothing (normal: JA cues are shorter and denser)
            BORROWS the EN cue it overlaps most and is flagged enShared so the UI
            can dim it - the learner is told the English is not a line-for-line gloss.
            A JA cue overlapping no EN at all gets null, never a wrong translation.
   Complexity O(n+m). Degrades correctly to all-null when there is no EN track. */
export function align(ja,en){
  if(!en||!en.length) return ja.map(c=>({...c,en:null}));
  const owners=new Map();
  let j=0;
  for(const ec of en){
    while(j+1<ja.length && ja[j].e<=ec.s) j++;
    let best=-1,bestOv=0;
    for(let k=j;k<ja.length && ja[k].s<ec.e;k++){
      const o=ov(ja[k],ec);
      if(o>bestOv){bestOv=o;best=k;}
    }
    if(best>=0&&bestOv>0){ if(!owners.has(best)) owners.set(best,[]); owners.get(best).push(ec); }
  }
  return ja.map((c,i)=>{
    const own=owners.get(i);
    if(own&&own.length) return {...c,en:own.map(x=>x.t).join(" "),enShared:false};
    let best=null,bestOv=0;
    for(const ec of en){ if(ec.s>=c.e) break; const o=ov(c,ec); if(o>bestOv){bestOv=o;best=ec;} }
    return {...c, en:best?best.t:null, enShared:!!best};
  });
}

// timedtext RATE-LIMITS HARD (429) and the block lasts a long time.
// Serial + long exponential backoff is mandatory. Never parallelise this.
async function track(t){
  const u=new URL(t.baseUrl);
  u.searchParams.set("fmt","json3");   // MUST .set() - baseUrl already has fmt=srv3,
                                       // appending &fmt=json3 is IGNORED and returns XML
  let wait=20000;
  for(let a=0;a<8;a++){
    const r=await fetch(u.toString());
    if(r.status===429){ await sleep(wait); wait=Math.min(wait*1.5,120000); continue; }
    if(!r.ok) throw new Error("timedtext HTTP "+r.status);
    const body=await r.text();
    if(!body.length) throw new Error("empty caption body");
    return JSON.parse(body);
  }
  throw new Error("429 exhausted - wait and resume");
}

const tokenizer = await new Promise((res,rej)=>
  kuromoji.builder({dicPath:"node_modules/kuromoji/dict"}).build((e,t)=>e?rej(e):res(t)));

const NO_LOOKUP=new Set(["記号","助詞","助動詞","フィラー"]);
// Glue inflections/auxiliaries onto the content word: 読ん+で+い+ます -> 読んでいます
// Without this, a phone user gets 1-character tap targets and taps "ます" by accident.
function chunk(text){
  const raw=tokenizer.tokenize(text), out=[];
  for(const t of raw){
    const glue = t.pos==="助動詞"
              || (t.pos==="動詞" && t.pos_detail_1==="非自立")
              || (t.pos==="助詞" && t.pos_detail_1==="接続助詞")
              || t.pos_detail_1==="接尾";
    if(glue && out.length && out[out.length-1].base){ out[out.length-1].w += t.surface_form; continue; }
    out.push({
      w:t.surface_form,
      base: NO_LOOKUP.has(t.pos) ? null : (t.basic_form!=="*" ? t.basic_form : t.surface_form),
      pos:t.pos,
      read: (t.reading && t.reading!=="*") ? t.reading : null
    });
  }
  return out;
}

   6. player.js - YouTube IFrame integration for a mobile PWA
   ============================================================================ */
const YT_UNSTARTED=-1, YT_ENDED=0, YT_PLAYING=1, YT_PAUSED=2, YT_BUFFERING=3, YT_CUED=5;

let apiReady=null;
function loadYT(){
  if(apiReady) return apiReady;
  apiReady=new Promise(res=>{
    if(window.YT && window.YT.Player) return res(window.YT);
    window.onYouTubeIframeAPIReady=()=>res(window.YT);
    const s=document.createElement("script");
    s.src="https://www.youtube.com/iframe_api";  // needs network; see offline fallback below
    document.head.appendChild(s);
  });
  return apiReady;
}

export class WatchPlayer {
  /** cues: [{s,e,ja,en,tk}] with times in MILLISECONDS */
  constructor({mount, videoId, cues, onCue, onState}){
    Object.assign(this,{mount,videoId,cues,onCue,onState});
    this.i=-1; this.raf=0; this.last=0;
  }

  async init(){
    const YT=await loadYT();
    this.p=new YT.Player(this.mount,{
      videoId:this.videoId,
      host:"https://www.youtube-nocookie.com",  // no cookies set until playback starts
      playerVars:{
        playsinline:1,      // REQUIRED. Without it iOS hijacks into native fullscreen
                            // and your entire subtitle UI disappears.
        controls:1,         // keep YouTube's controls: ToS-friendly and scrubbing works
        rel:0, modestbranding:1,
        cc_load_policy:0,   // hide YouTube's own captions - ours ARE the feature
        iv_load_policy:3,
        origin:location.origin, enablejsapi:1
      },
      events:{
        onReady:()=>this.onState?.("ready"),
        onStateChange:e=>this._state(e.data),
        // 2 bad param | 5 html5 error | 100 removed/private | 101 & 150 embedding disabled
        onError:e=>this.onState?.("error:"+e.data)
      }
    });
  }

  _state(s){
    this.onState?.(s);
    if(s===YT_PLAYING) this._start(); else this._stop();
    if(s===YT_PLAYING||s===YT_PAUSED||s===YT_ENDED) this._tick(true); // settle after a seek
  }

  /* --- 10fps sync: rAF gated to 100ms, running ONLY while actually playing ---
     Ungated rAF is 60fps and pointless (100ms is below perception for subtitles).
     rAF beats setInterval because the browser suspends it on a hidden tab. */
  _start(){ if(!this.raf) this.raf=requestAnimationFrame(this._loop); }
  _stop(){ if(this.raf){ cancelAnimationFrame(this.raf); this.raf=0; } }
  _loop=(ts)=>{
    this.raf=requestAnimationFrame(this._loop);
    if(ts-this.last<100) return;
    this.last=ts; this._tick(false);
  };

  _tick(force){
    if(!this.p?.getCurrentTime) return;
    const ms=this.p.getCurrentTime()*1000;    // locally interpolated, cheap to call
    const n=this._find(ms);
    if(n!==this.i||force){ this.i=n; this.onCue?.(n, n>=0?this.cues[n]:null); }
  }

  /* cursor hint first (O(1) while playing), binary search after a seek */
  _find(ms){
    const c=this.cues;
    if(this.i>=0){
      const cur=c[this.i];
      if(cur && ms>=cur.s && ms<cur.e) return this.i;
      const nx=c[this.i+1];
      if(nx && ms>=nx.s && ms<nx.e) return this.i+1;
    }
    let lo=0,hi=c.length-1;
    while(lo<=hi){ const m=(lo+hi)>>1;
      if(ms<c[m].s) hi=m-1; else if(ms>=c[m].e) lo=m+1; else return m; }
    return -1;
  }

  // SAFE from any context - pausing is never gesture-gated. This is what makes
  // "tap a word -> video stops -> explanation sheet opens" work reliably.
  pause(){ this.p?.pauseVideo?.(); }
  // GESTURE-GATED on iOS: only call from inside a real touch/click handler.
  play(){ this.p?.playVideo?.(); }

  seekMs(ms,play=false){ this.p?.seekTo?.(ms/1000,true); this.i=-1; this._tick(true); if(play) this.play(); }
  replayCue(){ const c=this.cues[this.i]; if(c) this.seekMs(c.s,true); }
  prevCue(){ if(this.i>0) this.seekMs(this.cues[this.i-1].s,true); }
  nextCue(){ if(this.i<this.cues.length-1) this.seekMs(this.cues[this.i+1].s,true); }
  setRate(r){ this.p?.setPlaybackRate?.(r); }   // 0.75 and 0.5 are gold for listening practice
  destroy(){ this._stop(); this.p?.destroy?.(); }
}

function onWordTap(token, cue, player){
  player.pause();                 // always works, no gesture needed
  openWordSheet({
    surface: token.w,
    lookup:  token.base,          // dictionary form -> OpenJLPT / JMdict
    reading: token.read,
    context: { videoId: player.videoId, ms: cue.s, sentence: cue.ja, gloss: cue.en }
  });
}

risks: The 48 business/story/N1 candidates in code_or_data are NOT verified to the same standard as the 131. I confirmed each has a manual Japanese caption track via the player API (HTTP 200), but the 429 block prevented downloading their cue bodies. Bake and inspect each one before shipping it; expect a few to disappoint.

Do NOT overlay subtitles on the iframe. YouTube's Required Minimum Functionality terms forbid 'overlays, frames, or other visual elements in front of any part of a YouTube embedded player'. This is not a style preference - it is the term that governs whether your embeds stay allowed. Subtitles go below the player.

Do not parallelise caption fetching. I proved concurrency 8 gets 586/586 HTTP 429 and the block on the IP outlasted 30+ minutes of backoff. Serial, >=2s apart, resumable (skip already-baked files), ideally run overnight and commit the results.

The `&fmt=json3` trap is silent, not loud. You get HTTP 200 with XML instead of JSON, so a naive JSON.parse throws somewhere unrelated and looks like a parsing bug. Always URL.searchParams.set('fmt','json3').

Caption baseUrls expire in ~7 hours and are IP/signature bound. If any code path stores a baseUrl and fetches it later, it will work in dev and fail in production the next day. Store only the baked cue text.
Never ship kuromoji or its 17MB dictionary to the phone. If you find yourself adding a runtime tokenizer to a PWA that must work offline, you have taken a wrong turn - tokenize at build time.

The catalog leans on a handful of channels: にほんごのじかん supplies most of N1 and a large share of N5/N3, Bite Size Japanese most of N2. If one channel deletes its back catalogue or turns off captions, a whole level thins out at once. The 48 candidates are the cheapest diversification.

JLPT level labels are approximate. About half came from the creator's own title (【N5】, N3・N2レベル, 'Advanced'); the rest I assigned from sampled cue text and speech register. JLPT grades vocabulary and grammar, not speech speed, so treat level as a sortable hint the user can override, not ground truth.
Videos with enTrack:false will show empty English on every line. Do not put one of those in onboarding or the app looks broken on first run - lead with the 63 bilingual ones.

Two Nihongo-Learning videos (Jh2C7JlWGKU, J62Y_9kuP_k) put a full kana transcription on a second line inside the cue. Rendered raw this looks like duplicated text. Split on the newline and treat the kana as a reading.

The IFrame API script itself must load from youtube.com, so the video screen cannot work fully offline even though the cues are cached. Detect failure to load and fall back to reading mode rather than showing a permanently spinning player.

kuromoji is IPADIC-based and mis-segments some keigo: 本日はお忙しい中... tagged お忙しい and いただき as 名詞. Word lookups will occasionally miss on honorific forms. Fall back to a substring match against your JMdict index when the base form misses, and consider hand-correcting tokens on the business videos.

playVideo() is gesture-gated on iOS but pauseVideo() is not. Auto-advance features that try to resume playback from a timer (not a tap) will silently fail on iPhone. Design any 'auto-continue' flow to require one tap.
